item.title: Man City Make Significant Change to Pre-Match Preparations for Fulham Clash
item.description: Man City Make Significant Change to Pre-Match Preparations for Fulham Clash MATCH PREVIEW: Manchester City vs Fulham (Premier League) More Videos The Premier League giants will be looking to bounce back from a notably poor run in the English top-flight after the final international break of the calendar year as Fulham visit the Etihad Stadium. Prior to the latest pause for national team commitments, Manchester City followed up a record-breaking seven successive wins to start Enzo Maresca's era at the club with three defeats in a row. Aston Villa were the side to break that run with a 2-1 victory at Villa Park, before Brighton & Hove Albion took all three points from the Etihad in a 0-1 win, and Nottingham Forest scored their first home goals of the season with a 3-1 triumph at the City Ground. Those results leave Manchester City in third behind the aforementioned Seagulls and Premier League champions Arsenal , who hold a six-point advantage over the Sky Blues coming into the next portion of domestic fixtures. And as Enzo Maresca and Manchester City look to end a run of poor results on the pitch, changes have seemingly been made to the way the club prepare for matchday action at the Etihad Stadium. That is according to TNT Sports' broadcast of Manchester City against Fulham on Saturday lunchtime, with Enzo Maresca and his squad staying overnight at The Medlock Hotel within the Etihad Campus and connected to the Etihad Stadium itself ahead of matchday.

item.title: Stephen A. Smith admits ‘special’ player has changed his MVP vote recently
item.description: Photo by Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images The talk around who is leading the way for the MVP award is already heating up, with a number of players proving themselves to be playing at the absolute elite level. There are several players who fall into the conversation, but the two main names, for many people, are Brock Purdy and Joe Burrow. Josh Allen is certainly still in the conversation, but Stephen A. Smith has narrowed it down to the quarterbacks for the San Francisco 49ers and the Cincinnati Bengals. Smith had previously claimed his vote would go to Purdy following his excellent start to the season. However, the ESPN analyst has now admitted he has changed his mind over recent weeks and would give Burrow the advantage. Stephen A. Smith changes his MVP decision to Joe Burrow If the voting was now, it would be incredibly difficult to separate these two quarterbacks, with both of them showing their quality through the first half of the season. The advantages could be earned through their upcoming matchups against their expected postseason rivals. “Three weeks ago, it would have been Brock Purdy. I think Brock Purdy has been big-time this year. What I’m seeing from Joe Burrow right now, though, is special,” Smith said on First Take. “When I watch Joe Burrow throw this football, the man is just special. When he’s lined up behind centre, he’s a true difference-maker. You can see why Cincinnati went to back-to-back AFC Championship games and reached a Super Bowl with him as quarterback. Again, I’ve been Brock Purdy, Brock Purdy, Brock Purdy all season long because of the way he’s been playing, and I know he hasn’t had Mike Evans, which is another reason why I would give him the edge.” Burrow has led the Bengals to a five-game winning streak, with some favourable games ahead of them before the end of the season. A meeting with Patrick Mahomes in December is one many will have marked on their calendars, though. “When you look at Joe Burrow, though: A fifth consecutive game with at least four total touchdowns (the only other quarterback in NFL history to accomplish that was Peyton Manning in 2004). Seven consecutive games completing better than 70% of his passes,” Smith added. “It’s a phenomenal thing to watch right now, and the Cincinnati Bengals are winning football games. Taking all of that into consideration, Josh Allen and Brock Purdy obviously come to mind, but right now, I’ve got to give Joe Burrow the edge.” Read more: Jimmy Pitaro told what he must do right away to end the Troy Aikman and Joe Buck drama Dianna Russini shares seven words her NFL connections are telling her about Daniel Jones’ release by Indianapolis Colts ‘He’s done’ – Stephen A. item.title: Lehmann again denies knowing about sandpaper plot
item.description: Darren Lehmann is currently head coach of Northamptonshire [Getty Images] Former Australia coach Darren Lehmann has again vehemently denied any knowledge of the sandpaper plot, despite detailed allegations from Cameron Bancroft. In an ongoing row about the cheating scandal that took place in Australia's third Test against South Africa in 2018, Bancroft published a testimony running to more than 4,000 words in the West Australian newspaper on Wednesday. At the same time, Lehmann was commentating on Australia's third one-day international against England, with Bancroft's account prompting him to leave the match early. On Saturday, Lehmann returned to broadcast for the BBC and Australian network ABC on the first T20 international in Melbourne. In an extended and emotional interview, addressing a range of Bancroft's claims, Lehmann said: He "didn't know" sandpaper was used by his Australia team. No coaches encouraged players to tamper with the ball before or during Australia's tour of South Africa in 2018. He is "not sure" about a walkie-talkie conversation with 12th man Peter Handscomb, which Bancroft claimed was an instruction from Lehmann to remove the sandpaper from the field. He resigned as Australia coach before he was sacked and did not sign a non-disclosure agreement. The fallout from the sandpaper scandal took him to a "really dark place". Cummins' integrity not compromised - CA Cummins' Australia captaincy at a crossroads - Agnew Bancroft sandpaper claims heap pressure on Cummins Lehmann's renewed denial came on the same day Cricket Australia confirmed its "unanimous support" for Pat Cummins as Australia captain. Earlier, Cummins' fellow fast bowler Josh Hazlewood said he would consider his international future if the captain was forced to stand down. The debate about the sandpaper plot of 2018 was reopened two weeks ago by allegations in the autobiography of Usman Khawaja, who was part of the Australia team in Cape Town eight years ago. Khawaja's assertions that the whole team knew and should have taken responsibility have been supported by David Warner, Chadd Sayers and Jon Holland, who were all on the tour. Warner, former captain Steve Smith and Bancroft were the only players punished for the cheating plot. It was Bancroft's testimony that heaped pressure on Lehmann, Cummins and the other members of the Australia team who played at Newlands. Cummins, Hazlewood and the rest of the Australia bowlers who played in Cape Town have always denied knowledge or involvement in the plan to use sandpaper on the ball. Lehmann resigned as coach in the immediate aftermath of the South Africa tour, but the former Australia batter has always maintained his innocence. "Sandpaper, I didn't know," he said on Saturday. "Obviously, it was used. "The biggest thing with ball-tampering is it was just a bad time. Everyone, we all made mistakes. "But you've just got to try and move on. I know it's hard for everyone. item.title: Reacts Results: Win and you’re in their hearts
item.description: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 16: Jacoby Brissett #11 of the Baltimore Ravens warms up prior to the game against the Los Angeles Chargers at M&T Bank Stadium on November 16, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images All it took is one skin-of-their-teeth win over the New Orleans Saints to end a three-game losing skid, seize first place in the NFC South, and restore some faith from fans for the 4-5 Carolina Panthers. It helps, of course, that they are facing, at home, a 4-6 Baltimore Ravens team who is on their own five-game losing streak and is 1-5 in their last six games since Lamar Jackson was injured the first time for the season. This week they are giving newly acquired Jacoby Brissett his second start at quarterback for the Ravens and we’re all going to see what happens after that. Confidence rising 26% after a win in which the team arguably played a less complete game than they did in their loss to the Denver Broncos the week before has me wondering if this survey is just a lagging indicator of wins. They are the division leader with the worst record, with the NFC East leading New York Giants coming in as a close second at 5-3-1. Third place is a four way tie of 7-2 teams, including the Detroit Lions who currently sit atop a three-way 7-2 tie in the NFC North. There is no wonder we are seeing a lot of contemplation about changes to the playoff format when the Panthers are on track for a home playoff game (or whoever ‘wins’ the NFC South) and the NFC North is likely to have one or more teams with winning records miss the playoffs entirely. As for this week, most fans are unsurprisingly expecting a win. The Ravens have suffered injuries both natural and self-inflicted—looking at you, Marlon Humphrey—and are struggling to find a quarterback solution to keep their own playoff hopes on life support. The path to a wildcard berth is more open in the AFC, but extremely unlikely all the same. Have the Ravens given up as a team? Are they simply hopeless without Jackson? Are the Carolina Panthers capable of resurrecting any team’s lost pride and dignity with a surprisingly competitive game? A disciplined Panthers squad that is getting healthier are catching the ailing Ravens at the perfect time. Whether or not that is what we see on Sunday is anybody’s guess. item.title: Why Skip Bayless ‘can’t believe’ his own prediction for 49ers vs Vikings
item.description: Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images Skip Bayless has admitted he ‘can’t believe’ that he is backing the Minnesota Vikings to beat the San Francisco 49ers because that would mean Kirk Cousins wins a big game. The 49ers are 8-1 this season, with the Vikings not far behind them in the NFC with a 7-2 record. Minnesota have the best defence in the league this year and while they were previously struggling on the offence, they have now added Cousins as their new starting quarterback. The 38-year-old was in good form for the Las Vegas Raiders prior to his trade but Bayless does not seem to rate him when it comes to showing up in big games. In turn, he admitted on First Take that he ‘can’t believe’ he has picked the Vikings to win on Sunday. Bayless said: “The Minnesota Vikings will win this game. And I can’t believe I just said that because that means that Kirk Cousins will win a big game.” 2026 Minnesota Vikings are perfect for Kirk Cousins Cousins has struggled to perform in the postseason throughout his career. He has a 1-4 record and is 1-3 as the starting quarterback. However, Bayless also thinks that this Minnesota team is actually perfect for the ex-Raiders star due to their impressive defence. He continued: “I have spent 15 years saying Kirk Cousins is way overrated and way, way, way overpaid. Wait, he’s made more money than Tom Brady. “He’s 1 and 4 in the postseason. Dak was 4-0 against him when he was in Washington. But now, at age 38, Kirk Cousins has almost magically fallen into the perfect spot for him with the NFL’s best defence and the ability to reach back, recreate, turn back the clock to 2022 when those Vikings with Kirk Cousins at quarterback went 13-4 and Justin Jefferson was the offensive player of the year.” They have given up just 126 points this season, which is the best record in the league by some distance. Minnesota Vikings: 126 Jacksonville Jaguars: 144 Kansas City Chiefs: 156 Seattle Seahawks: 175 Tampa Bay Buccaneers: 178 Their only real issue this season has been the offence. But while he has only played one game so far, Cousins seems to have had an immediate impact. He helped the Vikings score 30 points against the Green Bay Packers last week, which was the first time they scored 30-plus in a game since the opening week of 2026/27. item.title: Juventus must focus on May, not August
item.description: TURIN, ITALY - NOVEMBER 18: Juventus head coach Luciano Spalletti during a Juventus FC training session at JTC on November 18, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Filippo Alfero - Juventus FC/Juventus FC via Getty Images) | Juventus FC via Getty Images Here’s a question right off the bat: Coming out of the international break and looking at the rest of the 2026-27 season ahead, what is the best way Juve can make the most of their remaining fixtures? Too often Juventus have approached transfer windows as opportunities to solve every problem, everywhere, all at once. Though, I accept, what we have seen as the problem has not always been what they have seen as the problem, and let’s not even start on what the “solutions” have looked like on some occasions. Perhaps I am best left, at this early stage, to posit that our transfer mentality has not always lead us to greener pastures. This January needs to be different. Looking to start our run for the rest of the year now, we need to be strategic and ruthless when it comes to the next couple of months. Bluntly, our objective is not to build the Juventus of 2029 in the next six weeks. That ship has sailed — and I think we can all agree that it has floundered somewhat mid-journey. It is not even to build the Juventus of next season. I think the best, the clearest, the most ruthless thing we can do now is to maximize the Juventus that takes the field between February and May. Every decision, whether tactical, sporting, or financial, should be judged against a simple question: Will this help Juventus win more points during over the next six weeks and then into the second half of this season? If the answer is no, it can wait. Before we even think about making signings, we need to understand exactly what we already have, and what we are going to do with it. Several key questions must be answered before Christmas. The first concerns Kenan Yıldız. This young man has shown flashes of brilliance, he stands ready to become the face of the club. But — how many times have we read that word in conjunction with Juve — there is a significant difference between a prospect and a star. If Yıldız is ready to become the centerpiece of the attack, recruitment should focus on supporting him. If he is not yet at that stage, Juventus may need additional firepower. The second sits with Khéphren Thuram. Perhaps no player embodies the future more than this midfielder. If Thuram establishes himself as one of Serie A’s elite midfielders, the club gains a foundational piece around which a title-winning side can be built. If not, resources may need to be allocated differently. The management team should spend the weeks before January evaluating the squad with complete honesty. Championship challenges are built on clarity, not hope. Which brings us to goals — or the lack of them. item.title: How McLaren tried to mitigate its Las Vegas F1 top speed deficit
item.description: Motorsport photo Despite what was a respectable result on a circuit that accentuated the MCL40's flaws without rewarding its virtues, Lando Norris was not best pleased with how Friday at the Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend. “We're just shocking on the straights,” said Norris shortly after qualifying fifth, just under eight tenths behind polesitter Kimi Antonelli, who is set to drop five places for an engine penalty, elevating Norris to fourth on the grid. The long straights and low downforce demands meant the Las Vegas Strip circuit was never going to be the strongest track for this car, as foreshadowed by McLaren's muted form on the circuit's nearest comparisons in Monza and Baku. But McLaren's deficit in Vegas was still surprisingly vast, at least to Antonelli, with Norris and Oscar Piastri routinely 20km/h down on the circuit's long Las Vegas Boulevard as well as the final straight towards the finish. Differences so massive are rarely just down to one single factor, and that also proved to be the case on Friday. Despite regular upgrades, the MCL40 remains relatively draggy and aerodynamically inefficient, which is compounded by the team's pre-season choice to go for a shorter gearing, costing it top-end grunt on circuits with extremely long straights. Like all teams, McLaren had the option to make one mid-season change to its gear ratios, but decided against it because its shorter gearing would still stand it in good stead on other circuits. In Vegas, though, the team had to pay the price. "Definitely we had some concern in terms of how suitable the demands of this circuit would be for our car," team principal Andrea Stella replied when asked by Motorsport.com whether the squad's deficit was more severe than anticipated. "This is not only the top speed, it is also the top speed that is combined with the towing that everyone is trying to do. So, you go in operating regimes of the engine that with our ratios is not ideal. We know that the drag from an aerodynamic point of view is not a point of strength. We have seen traits that are similar to Monza, to Baku. And in all conditions we were not particularly competitive." Lando Norris, McLaren Lando Norris, McLaren With slipstreaming so crucial, as evidenced by the positional tactics that dominated Q3 and cost the likes of Isack Hadjar and George Russell , McLaren tried to compensate for its lack of top speed by more aggressively chasing the tow. "What we have done better here is to mitigate this by having really good positioning," Stella added. "The car was pretty much where we wanted it to be in qualifying. And this definitely helped. Because I have to say that it seems like with these regulations the drag reduction when you follow one car or even multiple cars is more than in the past. And therefore, there is an even higher incentive to be positioned in the right place." item.title: JuJu Watkins issues WNBA draft update after dropping 36 points for USC
item.description: Photo by Melina Pizano/Getty Images Fresh off dropping 36 points for USC, JuJu Watkins finally addressed where she stands on the WNBA draft. JuJu Watkins didn’t take long to remind everyone why she’s the consensus No. 1 pick for the 2027 WNBA Draft. With the Toronto Tempo winning the draft lottery after their rough 11–33 debut season, mock drafts already have the expansion team locking in the USC star, assuming she actually declares. Coming off an ACL tear, Watkins erased any doubts in No. 4 USC’s 78–69 win over Baylor, taking over the game with 36 points, 11 rebounds, six steals, and four assists in 39 minutes. JuJu Watkins is still undecided on the WNBA Following the win, reporters inevitably asked JuJu Watkins about her plans for the 2027 WNBA Draft, and she made it clear she’s keeping her focus strictly on USC for now: She said: “I really can’t say what I’m doing because I don’t know. item.title: NCAA Tournament second round preview: No. 2-seed Maryland men’s soccer vs. NC State
item.description: After finishing the regular season with a 12-5-1 record and making it to the Big Ten tournament semifinals, No. 2-seed Maryland men’s soccer enters its 32nd NCAA tournament under head coach Sasho Cirovski. As the tournament begins, Cirovski is looking for the Terps to play their best soccer going forward. “I think it comes down to playing your best at the right time,” Cirovski said. “All year I’ve looked at some of our difficult moments as an opportunity to get stronger and tougher and I certainly hope that what we see at this point in the year.” The Terps hold home-field advantage for their second-round matchup against NC State. The game will be played at 1 p.m. Sunday at Ludwig Field and will be televised on ESPN Plus. “I think you’re seeing two elite teams,” Cirovski said. “I think it’s a very big matchup in the round of 32.” NC State (8-6-6, 1-3-4 ACC) In 2025, the Wolfpack had an outstanding season, finishing with a 16-3-4 record and making it all the way to the national championship. They ultimately fell to a Washington team that had knocked out Maryland earlier in the tournament. Donavan Phillip, who won the MAC Hermann Trophy after leading the nation with 19 goals, along with defender Nikola Markovic and goalkeeper Logan Erb departed in the offseason. Despite the roster turnover, NC State earned its third NCAA tournament appearance in as many years under head coach Marc Hubbard. This season, the Wolfpack faced more turbulence after finishing the regular season with a single conference win and the 11-seed in the ACC tournament. However, NC State defeated six-seed Virginia Tech and three-seed Wake Forest to make it to the semifinal before falling to the eventual champions, North Carolina. In the first round of the NCAA tournament, the Wolfpack defeated College of Charleston, 2-1, on Thursday after two second-half goals from Hayato Takayama and Tyler Caton. Entering Sunday’s match, NC State is unbeaten in eight of its last nine games, including a 3-1-3 record against six NCAA tournament teams during that stretch. item.title: Virgil van Dijk has ‘no idea’ whether he will extend contract at Liverpool
item.description: Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk remains uncertain of whether he will remain at the club beyond the end of the season. The 35-year-old centre-back is approaching the final six months of his contract , which expires next summer. He believes that he can keep playing at the top level for “many more years” but says he has “no idea” whether that will be at Anfield as Liverpool’s decision-makers continue to ponder over a fresh offer. "The main thing for me is that I feel good and I'm looking after myself and I still have many more years in my opinion," Van Dijk told Sky Sports. "Whatever's going to happen after this season, we'll see. At this moment of time, if anyone says that or put out that they know what I'm going to do next season, it's untrue because at this moment of time, speaking to you, I've got no idea either. "But I'm relaxed with it because if you know me, I only focus on what I can control and that's at the moment the Manchester United game. Then we'll focus to the Champions League and whatever happens in the new year coming, we'll see then. "But it's been an incredible journey, almost 10 years this summer and it's been a big part of my life and I'll forever be grateful for anything that happened over those years. "If it's getting extended, we'll see then. If not, then I'm going to say goodbyes in the summer." Virgil van Dijk’s future is up in the air with his contract expiring in the summer (Getty) Van Dijk has won two Premier League titles, including the club’s first in 30 years, as well as a Champions League with Liverpool, stamping his mark as one of the greatest centre-backs in the English top flight’s history since his £75m arrival from Southampton in 2018. He is one of the last remaining figures from Jurgen Klopp ’s side that won every trophy there was to win between 2019 and 2022, with Mohamed Salah and Andy Robertson notably bidding emotional farewells at the end of last season. Asked about the prospect of having to say goodbye to Anfield himself, Van Dijk said: " Well, yeah, probably for me the most and the family because it's been an incredible time. "But I don't look too far in the future and that's been, in my opinion, also a little bit of a success. I won't change it now either. "Whatever happens, happens. Let's see." Liverpool host Manchester United for new manager Mauricio Pochettino’s first game on Sunday afternoon.

item.title: 'That is the most ridiculous question to ask' - Ruud Gullit refuses to choose between Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo
item.description: GOLF-EPGA-NED - AFP Former Netherlands midfielder Ruud Gullit has refused to take sides in the long-running debate between Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, dismissing the comparison as ridiculous. The 1987 Ballon d'Or winner instead insisted he was simply glad to watch both superstars compete before steering the conversation towards Argentine legend Diego Maradona. Dutch icon rejects rivalry question Gullit pushed back when asked whether Messi or Ronaldo ranks higher during an appearance on Sports Uncensored . Host Simon Jordan closed their interview by pressing the former AC Milan star to name the better player. When reminded that Ballon d'Or voting demands one winner, the Dutchman declined to pick either man and cited an old rival instead. Gullit gives blunt studio response Few retired players escape being asked about the pair, and Gullit reacted immediately when Jordan raised the topic on the show: "Come on. No, that is the most ridiculous question to ask. I have seen these two battling each other for such a long, long time." Preferring to enjoy their rivalry rather than rank them, he explained: "I am happy that I've seen it. Both of them." When Jordan noted Gullit had once been named the best himself, he replied: "On that moment on, if you would ask me who was the best player when I won it, I would have said Diego Maradona." The host laughed and conceded the point was reasonable, though not what he wanted. Maradona remains his ultimate benchmark Naming Maradona was no improvisation from Gullit, who faced the Napoli talisman several times with Milan. During a tribute at The Best gala in December 2020 shortly after Maradona's death, he recalled: "I remember the first time I faced him. [Roberto] Donadoni and [Carlo] Ancelotti were trying to take the ball off him and couldn't. He was incredibly strong and technically brilliant. He was also a leader, always talking to his teammates so they would give more." Noting how opponents targeted him physically, Gullit said: "They tried to take him out of the game with kicks, and they managed it once, when Goikoetxea injured him." He added: "They couldn't stop him. Imagine if he had today's protection, the video, the cameras and all that. I faced him and I can say he is the best in history." Greatest player debate rolls on Comparisons between Messi and Ronaldo show no sign of fading among supporters and former players as their careers wind down. For Gullit, however, the standard for football's greatest was set decades ago by the opponent he battled firsthand in Serie A. Until anyone surpasses that memory, the Dutchman is unlikely to change his verdict.

item.description: (Mike Dinovo-Imagn Images) LAKE FOREST, Ill. — The Bears’ bye week is over. It’s back to football and a stretch run that includes four NFC North games. But first comes the New Orleans Saints at Soldier Field. “It’s all about winning this week,” coach Ben Johnson said. “We’ll worry about everything else when it’s time. It’s not time for that. There’s still eight games to be played and this is the most important one because it’s the next one.” With that in mind, here is everything you need to know about the Bears from the podium to the locker room to the injury report in Week 11. 1. Quarterback Caleb Williams doesn’t feel like he’s playing through an injury right now. But he’s still got to manage his right hamstring going forward. “Once you have a severe injury like that and you come back and you didn’t have it before, you have to keep consistently doing rehab over and over again throughout the weeks to be able to just keep it strong and keep it up to date and make it stronger to get back to where it was, because it takes a while,” he said. “It’s not being overworked or anything like that but (it’s) just being able to focus on it throughout the weeks.” The bye week certainly helped, too. “It was good,” Williams said. “It’s always good to get that time off. Especially since the injury, I’ve been go, go, go, whether it’s rehab, whether it’s film, whether it’s the games (and) obviously, the short weeks, the long weeks, anything like that, schedules changing around. “It was good to get some time off and reset mentally and physically. I didn’t do ‘nothing’ but just had a little bit more time to be able to relax and maybe not move as much.” 2. The bye week also came at the perfect time for receiver Luther Burden III. Burden suffered a concussion against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 9 at Soldier Field. But he passed all protocols by the time the team returned to practice on Monday. Burden practiced in full every day. He doesn’t have an injury designation for Sunday. “Luther’s huge for this offense,” quarterback Caleb Williams said on Tuesday. “I mean, he took a 40-, 50-yard, 60-yard pass to the crib on a 5-yard route. So that’s who Luther is. I talk about him each week that we get up here or anything like that that I get the chance to just because he’s special for us. He’s explosive, he makes plays, he’s going to keep making plays, he’s going to keep getting up and celebrating, bringing the energy and the juice for us as a team, as an offense. “And so him being cleared is exciting. item.description: Photo by Jordan Bank/Getty Images Gary Woodland had somewhat of a renaissance season in 2026. In 2023, he underwent brain surgery to remove a benign tumor from his brain, which was pressing against a part of his brain that controls fear responses. Woodland has since suffered from PTSD, which he opened up about this year. It’s mightily impressive, therefore, that the 42-year-old returned to winning ways this year, claiming victory at the Houston Open. He finished in the top five twice this season, and is now ranked in the top 50 in the world. Woodland’s play in 2026 earned him a place at Tiger Woods’ Hero World Challenge event in the Bahamas, but unfortunately his health struggles have continued to end the year. He withdrew from the tournament and took to social media to explain the reason why. Gary Woodland explains withdrawal from Hero World Challenge Luckily, Woodland’s withdrawal has nothing to do with his 2023 brain surgery. Instead, it’s a knee injury that required surgery and has ruled him out of Woods’ event. The 2019 US Open winner took to social media to explain his withdrawal: “Just a brief health update for everyone (don’t worry, my brain is fine!). item.title: Caleb Wilson shares when he’ll be back playing for the Chicago Bulls after fracturing his hand
item.description: Photo by Daniel Bartel/Getty Images Caleb Wilson was the talk of the town in Chicago with his performances for the Bulls in the first few games of this season. The rookie played the first 10 games and averaged 18.9 points, 6.2 rebounds and 1.9 assists, and many have since viewed him as the future of the franchise. Wilson is currently sidelined due to an injury, but he is anticipating a quick return to action. Caleb Wilson says he will be back in a couple of weeks During a game against the San Antonio Spurs, Wilson fractured his right hand while swiping at the ball in Victor Wembanyama’s grip. The 20-year-old scored 15 points and recorded five rebounds before going off, and the injury was expected to keep him on the sidelines for some time. On Friday, Wilson spoke to reporters, and he claimed that it is not a long-term injury and that he should be back as early as in a couple of weeks. He said, as per Joel Lorenzi on X : “I looked down on my hand, and it was bent the wrong way. I knew something was up and I heard it. “I mean, it’s difficult, but it’s not long-term. I’ll play again in a couple of weeks. I’m not really worried about it. It gives me an opportunity to get in shape, learn more about the game from a different view on the bench. So I’m excited.” When pressed about his ‘couple of weeks’ timeline, Wilson backtracked a bit, but he still seemed confident that he would be back soon. He said: “I don’t have an expectation on the timeline, but I just expect to be playing soon. I don’t expect this to be season-ending or make me miss a whole bunch of games. “I expect to play whenever I feel good, and I feel like I’ll feel good in a good amount of time.” The Chicago Bulls haven’t had a good season at all, but they have picked up a few wins since Wilson suffered his injury and has been unavailable. With the rookie playing, the Bulls won just one of their first nine games. Since his absence, they have won three of their five fixtures. That being said, Wilson is an incredible talent, and despite what the numbers say, we think the Bulls are a far better side when he’s fit and available for them. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. item.description: We've got a dramatic day of MLS action on offer today as the 2026 regular season comes to an end. How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊 With all games in the the respective conferences kicking off at the same time, we should get some epic finishes around the East and West. Here is how it all shaped out. Western Conference Vancouver came into the day having already wrapped up top spot in the conference, but their win in Montréal meant they set single-season club records in both points (64) and wins (19). Meanwhile, coming into the night there were six teams fighting for three remaining playoff spots — those spots fell to Portland (7th), Seattle (8th), and Real Salt Lake (9th), with the latter two facing off in the play-in match. An impressive win from Dallas and a defeat for San Jose means the Texas outfit wrapped up second place in the conference. And finally, the LA Galaxy saw their campaign in bitter fashion, starting the night in control of 7th place, but finishing 11th and out of the playoffs after a defeat in Salt Lake City. Eastern Conference Most notably, Nashville SC set a new MLS regular season points record after dispatching Cincinnati this afternoon. Nashville's 77 points from 23 wins and eight draws sees them eclipse Inter Miami's record of 74 points. In the playoff race, a late win for Columbus in Chicago sent Antoine Griezmann and Orlando City into the play-in match, and the Crew into the top-seven in dramatic fashion. Elsewhere, Inter Miami let a 3-0 lead slip against Charlotte, who came roaring back to snatch a point. Heading into the playoffs, Miami have only won just one of their last three matches.
